reasoning: This is a direct application of the Pigeonhole Principle. We have 11 pigeons and only 10 holes (numbered 0–9). Each hole can hold at most one pigeon, meaning at most 10 pigeons can be placed in total. It is mathematically impossible to assign 11 pigeons to 10 holes without at least one hole containing more than one pigeon. Therefore, the problem is UNSATISFIABLE.
